title: /admin is 20 tabs grouped by data model inside one 1,683-line client component, so the three tasks an operator actually performs each cross three to seven of them
description:
The whole admin surface is one client component. `VALID_TABS` (app/admin/page.tsx:112-133) declares 20 destinations, `ActiveTab` (:152-172) repeats the same 20 as a union, and `NAV_GROUPS_RAW` (:689-835) sorts them into 6 groups: User Management (users, teams, admins), Security (access-rules, blocked-data, security-alerts, audit), Communications (broadcast, notifications, ai-chats, support-tickets), Content (content), Billing (billing-overview), System (settings, updater, backup, queue-status, error-logs, email-logs, engine-feedback). Every group name is a data-model noun, not a job. The System group alone holds 7 unrelated destinations that share nothing except not fitting elsewhere: an update installer, a backup runner, a scanner-queue gauge, two log viewers, a settings editor and a detection-tuning tool. Content is a group of one. Billing is a group of one. The panel body is 20 sibling `{activeTab === X && <Manager/>}` lines (:1182-1674) with no route split, and AUDIT-012#fe-11 already measured the cost: 22 eagerly imported managers in one 1,333 KB route. The growth is visible in the leftovers: a 31-entry toast-label map inlined at :530-562, a stale 5-tab table still exported from components/admin/config.ts:7-17 (AUDIT-013#dead-01), and an empty app/api/v3/admin/bulk directory (AUDIT-011#bulk-06).

Measured click cost of the three most common operator tasks today.

A) Resolve a support ticket that needs the requester's account state. 1 click Support in the nav, 2 click the ticket, 3 select and copy the requester email (support-inbox.tsx:253 renders `owner_email` as plain text, no link), 4 click Users in the nav (handleTabChange at :869-876 calls setSelectedUser(null) and rewrites the URL, so the open ticket is gone), 5 click the search box and paste, wait the 300 ms debounce at :599, 6 click the user row, 7 click Support again, 8 click the ticket again to re-read it. Seven clicks plus a copy-paste, and the ticket view is rebuilt from scratch twice.

B) The morning check, is anything wrong right now. The panel lands on `activeTab = "users"` (:203). Scanner Queue is 1 click, Error Logs 2, Security Alerts 3, Backups 4, Email Logs 5, Support 6. Six clicks, six panels that each refetch on mount with their own poll interval, and the operator does the staleness arithmetic on the backup date themselves. Only one of the 20 nav items carries any status indicator at all (the updater dot, :1087-1092).

C) Apply a support fix to one user, for example reset a daily scan limit. Type in the search box, 1 click the row, then scroll past Overview, Account Management, Staff Role and Badges and Admin Notes to reach Support Actions (user-detail-panel.tsx:1872), 2 click the right card out of 21 laid out in a `grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3` (:1894), 3 confirm. Three clicks, but the cost is scanning 21 near-identical cards, not the clicks.
impact: An operator cannot form a mental model of the panel from its navigation, because the navigation describes the database rather than the work. Cross-referencing is the normal case in support and the panel makes it the expensive case: task A costs seven clicks and destroys the operator's place twice. Task B, the one that protects the service, costs six clicks and is therefore skipped, which is how the failures AUDIT-012#obs-02 and AUDIT-012#obs-03 found stay invisible. New destinations get appended to whichever group is least wrong, so the drift compounds.
recommendation:
Regroup by operator job and split the route. Seven sections, 17 destinations, one home.

1. Operations (new default landing, replaces users as the initial tab at app/admin/page.tsx:203). Home view described in qols-02. Children: Scanner Queue, Error Logs, Email Logs, Backups, Updater. This merges the five System-group destinations that are all one question, is the machine healthy.
2. People. Users (search-first, see below), Teams, Staff and Invites (today's Active Staff plus the invite modal from staff-list.tsx).
3. Support. Tickets, AI Chats. Moves ai-chats out of Communications: reading a user's conversation is support and moderation work, not messaging.
4. Trust and Safety. Security Alerts, Access Rules, Blocked Data, Hosts and Shares (today's single-item Content group). Merges four scattered destinations into the one job, deciding what a user or an IP is allowed to do.
5. Billing. Billing Overview, plus a gifted-subscriptions list (today gifts are only visible per-user through user-detail-panel.tsx:2251).
6. Messaging. Broadcast, Notifications. Both are tell users something; today they sit in Communications next to two support tools.
7. Configuration. Settings, Engine Feedback, Audit Log.

Searchable rather than browsable: Users, Audit Log, Error Logs, Email Logs, AI Chats are all logs you query. Users should open on a search field with recent-activity results underneath, not a paginated directory of every account.

Mechanics: give each destination its own route segment under app/admin/(section)/, which deletes the 20-branch conditional at :1182-1674 and fixes AUDIT-012#fe-11 for free. Move the tab table out of app/admin/page.tsx into a single exported ADMIN_SECTIONS in components/admin/config.ts (replacing the stale ADMIN_TABS at config.ts:7-17), keyed by permission exactly as NAV_GROUPS_RAW already does, and derive VALID_TABS, ActiveTab and the mobile TOC from it.

After the restructure: task A becomes 1 click (the requester name in the ticket header opens an inline account panel, see qols-03) with zero navigation. Task B becomes 0 clicks, the home view is the landing page, and a click only to drill into whatever is red. Task C stays 3 clicks; the win there is time-to-find, addressed separately in qols-06.

title: The admin landing view is ten headcount aggregates, none of which can go red, so there is no screen anywhere that answers whether anything is wrong right now
description:
The panel opens on the users tab (app/admin/page.tsx:203) and the only thing above the user table is two StatBar rows of five counters each (:1108-1179): Total Users, Total Scans, Scans 24h, 2FA Enabled, Disabled, New Users 7d, Active API Keys, Active Webhooks, Schedules, Shared Scans. Every one is a plain COUNT from the stats query at app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:329-338. Not one can indicate a fault, and the code comment at app/admin/page.tsx:1103-1107 concedes they are not even clickable because the admin API takes only page, limit and search.

The signals that could go red exist but are each one nav click away and none is summarised anywhere. Scanner backlog: components/admin/features/queue-status-manager.tsx:72 computes `backedUp` and renders a destructive badge at :108-116, but only while that tab is mounted. Backup freshness: backup-manager.tsx:199-201 prints the newest file's mtime as plain text with no expected-interval comparison, so a backup that stopped running three weeks ago looks identical to one that ran this morning apart from a date the operator has to reason about. Security alerts, error logs, email delivery failures and support tickets are the same shape. Of the 20 nav items rendered at :1059-1094 exactly one carries a status indicator: the updater dot at :1087-1092.

This matters because AUDIT-012 found two failures that are silent by construction: #obs-02, a scheduled database backup that fails on every run still reports success to the failure escalator and writes no log line; #obs-03, worker failure escalation only sees pass-level throws, so a worker where every item failed resets its streak to zero and never alerts. Both are precisely the class of fault a health view exists to catch, and neither has any surface in the panel today.
impact: Nobody finds out the service is degraded from the admin panel. Backups can be dead for weeks (obs-02) and the Backups tab will show a stale date that reads as normal. A worker where every item errors (obs-03) shows no signal at all. The scanner queue can be backed up and the operator only learns when a user complains. On a service with about 50 real users and no on-call rotation, the admin panel is the whole monitoring story, and its front page is a vanity dashboard.
recommendation:
Add app/admin/(operations)/page.tsx as the panel's default landing view and change the initial activeTab at app/admin/page.tsx:203 to it. Render one status list, not a card grid: rows of `label / value / state`, each row green, amber or red, ordered worst-first, following the divided-list idiom in design-language.md D4 rather than adding a ninth stat strip. Rows to include, all buildable from endpoints that already exist:

- Scanner queue: reuse computeBackedUp and the stale-age thresholds already in components/admin/features/queue-status-utils.ts (STALE_PENDING_MS, STALE_RUNNING_MS). Red when backed up, amber when the oldest pending scan exceeds the stale threshold.
- Failed scans in the last 24 h: `counts.failedLast24h` from GET /api/v3/admin/queue-status. Amber above zero, red above a configurable share of completed.
- Backup age: from GET /api/v3/admin/backup's lastBackupAt, compared against the configured schedule interval rather than printed raw. Red when older than two intervals. This is the row that would have surfaced AUDIT-012#obs-02.
- Worker last success: add a per-worker last-success timestamp read and show age. This is the row that would have surfaced AUDIT-012#obs-03.
- Unresolved security alerts, error-log volume in the last hour, bounced or failed emails in the last 24 h, open support tickets, outstanding staff invites, update available.

Each row links to the tab that owns it. Mirror the worst state onto the nav item as a coloured dot, reusing the exact markup already at app/admin/page.tsx:1087-1092 so the operator sees a fault from any tab. Keep the ten headcount counters, but demote them to a collapsed Growth strip below the status list or move them to Billing Overview; they answer a business question, not an operational one.

title: The admin broadcast send loads every verified user with no LIMIT, then does two queries plus one SMTP round trip per recipient, sequentially
description: `const usersResult = await pool.query(userQuery, queryParams)` at app/api/v3/admin/features/route.ts:552 executes a query built from `SELECT u.id, u.email FROM users u WHERE u.email_verified_at IS NOT NULL` plus optional plan/preference filters -- no LIMIT, no batching, the whole verified user base materialized into Node memory. The loop at line 553 then runs, per recipient and strictly in order: a `SELECT 1 FROM broadcast_recipients WHERE message_id = $1 AND user_id = $2 AND status = 'sent' LIMIT 1` (line 558), an `await sendEmail(...)` (line 563), and an `INSERT INTO broadcast_recipients` (line 571). `broadcast_recipients` has only the separate single-column indexes `idx_broadcast_recipients_message` and `idx_broadcast_recipients_user` (instrumentation.ts:1160-1161), no `(message_id, user_id)` composite, so the dedupe check at 558 rescans one of those lists per iteration. The identical code is duplicated for the `resend` action at lines 714-743.
impact: Sending one broadcast to N users costs 1 + 2N database round trips and N sequential SMTP handshakes on a single pooled connection, inside one HTTP request. At today's ~50 users that is ~100 queries and a minute of blocking; the shape does not scale, and the request will time out long before the send finishes at any real size, leaving the broadcast half-delivered.
recommendation: Add `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_broadcast_recipients_msg_user ON broadcast_recipients(message_id, user_id);` and replace the per-row dedupe SELECT with a real UNIQUE constraint plus `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. Page the recipient query with `LIMIT`/keyset pagination and move the send itself to the background worker pattern already used by lib/scanner/scheduled-scans-worker.ts (`runInBatches`, line 393), which caps concurrency explicitly.

title: The admin 'update password' action enforces a hardcoded 8-character minimum, bypassing the admin-configurable PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH (12) and the strength gate every user-facing path applies
description: Every user-facing password path resolves the live setting and then runs the strength analyzer: app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:68-:72 and :88-:89, app/api/v3/auth/reset-password/route.ts:36-:41 and :46-:47, app/api/v3/auth/update/route.ts:316 and :301-:302, app/api/v3/auth/staff-invite/[token]/route.ts:156 and :170-:171. All four call getSetting('PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH') (default CONFIG_PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH = 12, lib/config/config-values.ts:314, admin-editable at lib/config/registry.ts:2130) and reject analyzePassword(pw).score < 3. The admin case 'update_password' at app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:732-:753 does neither: it validates only `typeof newPassword !== 'string' || newPassword.length < 8`, hashes, writes, and revokes sessions. There is no getSetting call and no analyzePassword call anywhere in that branch.
impact: On a deployment where the operator raised PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH to meet a policy, an admin resetting a user's password can still set an 8-character password, and 'Password123' passes because the analyzer never runs. The account then holds a credential the deployment's own configured policy forbids, and the audit log records it as a normal update_password action.
recommendation: In app/api/v3/admin/route.ts's update_password case, replace the literal 8 with `await getSetting('PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH')` and add the same `analyzePassword(newPassword).score < 3` rejection the other four routes use, so all five password write paths share one policy.

title: GET /api/v3/admin?section=user-detail has no permission gate, so the ops role reads any user's PII, sessions and IPs without VIEW_USERS
description: app/api/v3/admin/route.ts's GET gates only on requireStaff() at :81, which passes for any role at or above STAFF_ROLE_HIERARCHY.support = 10 (lib/config/client-constants.ts:39-49; ops/billing/security_analyst/content_manager are all 20). Two of its five sections then check nothing further: `section === "user-detail"` at :130 and the default stats+user-list branch at :325. The audit and active-admins sections DO gate, on hasStaffPermission(session.role, VIEW_AUDIT_LOG) at :249 and :294, which is the pattern the others are missing. user-detail returns, for any userId: email, role, plan, stripe_customer_id, subscription_status, google/github/discord identity columns, every active session row with ip_address and user_agent (:180-183), every api_keys row with prefix/limits (:168-171), webhooks, scheduled scans and internal admin notes. The ops role's grant list (lib/auth/permissions-client.ts:181-191) contains neither VIEW_USERS nor VIEW_USER_SESSIONS; billing (:145) and content_manager (:170) hold VIEW_USERS but not VIEW_USER_SESSIONS, yet all of them receive the session IP list. AUDIT-011#drift-18 flagged the matching UI cards in user-detail-panel.tsx; this is the API behind them, which a direct request reaches regardless of what the UI renders.
impact: Any of the four narrow specialist staff roles - which exist precisely so an ops or content person can reach one admin tab without user data - can read every user's email, billing identifiers, linked social accounts and last-known IP addresses by calling one URL. On a ~50-user production instance that is the entire user base's PII available to a role the operator deliberately scoped away from it.
recommendation: In app/api/v3/admin/route.ts, gate the user-detail branch (:130) and the default user-list branch (:325) on hasStaffPermission(session.role, STAFF_PERMISSIONS.VIEW_USERS) the same way :249 gates on VIEW_AUDIT_LOG, and drop the `activeSessions` key from the user-detail response (or the whole `sessionsRes` query) unless the caller also holds VIEW_USER_SESSIONS. Add the missing VIEW_BADGES gate to the badges branch at :281 while there.

title: Staff invite emails link to /staff-invite/[token], a page that does not exist, so no staff invite can ever be accepted
description: app/api/v3/admin/staff-invites/route.ts:134 builds `const inviteLink = `${APP_URL}/staff-invite/${token}`` and emails it (staffInviteEmail at :135). There is no app/staff-invite directory anywhere under app/ - the only matches for "staff-invite" are the two API route directories - so that URL 404s. The backing API pair app/api/v3/auth/staff-invite/[token]/route.ts exists and is fully implemented (GET validates a token without consuming it, POST accepts it and promotes or creates the account in one transaction), and its header at :22-30 calls itself "Public accept endpoints for a staff invite" - yet it is also absent from PUBLIC_PATHS, so even a hand-built page would be 307'd to /login for the invitee who has no account yet, which is the whole point of an invite. The admin-side UI is shipped and working: components/admin/staff/staff-list.tsx:117-127 lists pending invites and the modal creates them.
impact: Every staff invite an admin sends produces an email whose only call to action is a 404. There is no fallback path: the accept endpoints have no other caller. Adding staff therefore still requires an admin to edit the target account's role by hand in the admin panel, and the invite table accumulates rows nobody can act on.
recommendation: Build app/staff-invite/[token]/page.tsx: GET /api/v3/auth/staff-invite/[token] to show the invited email and role, then POST to accept (with a password field when the account does not exist yet, matching that route's POST contract). Add "/staff-invite" and "/api/v3/auth/staff-invite" to PUBLIC_PATHS in lib/config/public-paths.ts, beside the existing ROUTES.TEAMS_JOIN entry at :191 which exists for the identical "invitee has no account yet" reason.

title: BETA_ENABLED / BETA_BANNER_MESSAGE admin settings are fully wired to the UI but have zero functional consumer
description: lib/config/registry.ts defines BETA_ENABLED and BETA_BANNER_MESSAGE as runtime-tier settings, documented in app/docs/config/page.tsx as a real feature and given admin-panel display treatment. Nothing anywhere calls getSetting to gate or render anything with them. Not a regression (already dead before this session) but the registry migration gave dead functionality a real, documented, editable admin UI with no indication it's a no-op.
recommendation: Either wire a real beta-banner component that reads these two settings, or remove them from the registry/docs/admin UI until there's a consumer.

title: 4 admin routes bypass logAuditAction (audit-log regression)
description: After AUDIT-001 added logAuditAction with email redaction, 4 admin sites still use raw pool.query to insert audit log rows. The plain emails (team.owner_email, etc.) leak into the 365-day-retained details column.
recommendation: Replace raw INSERT INTO admin_audit_log calls with logAuditAction() helper from lib/auth/authorization.ts.

title: Seven admin row-action buttons are rendered at opacity-0 with only a hover trigger, so keyboard focus lands on invisible controls
description: These row-action controls use `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` with no focus variant: components/admin/teams/teams-list.tsx:483, :496, :514; components/admin/features/ip-rules-manager.tsx:804, :819; components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:1834; components/admin/audit/audit-log.tsx:462. `opacity-0` does not remove an element from the tab order, so the buttons stay focusable while remaining invisible, and the global focus ring at app/globals.css:370 is painted on a fully transparent element. Twenty-seven other hover-reveal sites in the same admin panel already pair the hover trigger with `group-focus-within:opacity-100` or `focus-visible:opacity-100` (for example components/admin/features/security-alerts-manager.tsx:367, components/admin/notifications/notifications-manager.tsx:625, app/admin/page.tsx:1463), so the fix pattern is established and these seven were just missed.
impact: A staff member tabbing through a team or IP-rule list hits stops where nothing is visible, including a delete action at teams-list.tsx:514, with no indication of what is focused or what Enter would do. WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.7. Admin-only, so low.
recommendation: Append `group-focus-within:opacity-100 focus-visible:opacity-100` to each of the seven className strings, matching components/admin/features/security-alerts-manager.tsx:367.

title: Eleven distinct confirmation implementations exist, including two raw window.confirm calls in the extension and eight ad-hoc rebuilds of the same AlertDialog
description: Eleven separate confirmation mechanisms are in use. Five are shared components: the Radix primitive components/ui/alert-dialog.tsx, rebuilt ad hoc with its own header, footer and state machine in eight places (app/shares/page.tsx:203, app/teams/page.tsx:648, app/history/page.tsx:640, components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:809, components/profile/tabs/developer/domains-section.tsx:479, components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:807, components/profile/tabs/profile-social-tab.tsx:260 and :826); components/admin/shared/confirm-dialog.tsx, a complete documented generic used only inside components/admin; components/admin/shared/admin-password-confirm-dialog.tsx; components/shared/save-confirmation-modal.tsx; and a plain components/ui/dialog.tsx pressed into service as a confirmation at components/profile/tabs/profile-security-tab.tsx:1695. Six are bespoke one-offs: a hand-rolled overlay at components/profile/tabs/profile-billing-tab.tsx:1532, the inline danger-zone panel at components/profile/tabs/profile-privacy-tab.tsx:480, three inline expand-in-place password panels at components/profile/tabs/profile-security-tab.tsx:814, :911 and :1308, a nested inline confirm at components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:1576, a two-click "click again" pattern at components/admin/users/gift-subscription-modal.tsx:191, and raw window.confirm at extension/src/options/options.ts:199 and :1101, the only two in the codebase. Recorded here so the next audit does not re-derive it: the two most dangerous user-facing actions are correctly gated hardest, account deletion requiring both a typed DELETE and the current password (components/profile/tabs/profile-privacy-tab.tsx:502-537) and clear-history naming the exact scan count in its copy (app/history/page.tsx:659-664). Merged from qols-05, which additionally documents that the admin panel alone chooses between three different confirmation dialog components depending on the action.
impact: Eight copies of one dialog is eight places to fix when the copy, busy behaviour or focus handling changes, and it is why some handle failure and others cannot: app/history/page.tsx:667-669 renders clearError inside the dialog, while components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:809 has nowhere to put an error, which is part of why qolf-04 exists. The extension's window.confirm renders unstyled OS chrome inside an otherwise themed options page.
recommendation: Move components/admin/shared/confirm-dialog.tsx to components/shared/confirm-dialog.tsx unchanged, add an optional error slot rendered above the footer the way app/history/page.tsx:667-669 does, and replace the eight ad-hoc AlertDialog call sites with it. The confirm-action registry in components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:85-118 and :431-453, one ConfirmAction union plus one getConfirmCopy function covering four destructive actions, is the right shape and should be the model for the teams and history call sites. Replace the two window.confirm calls in extension/src/options/options.ts with the extension's own dialog markup. Where qolf-09 introduces undo for an action, remove that action's confirmation at the same time rather than shipping both.

title: Five bespoke admin loading skeletons are exported through the shared barrel and rendered nowhere, so every admin section falls back to the generic skeletons
description: components/admin/shared/skeleton.tsx defines nine exports. Four are live: Skeleton (line 10), StatBarSkeleton (143), SettingsFieldsSkeleton (161) and DataTableSkeleton (184), used from components/admin/admin-skeleton.tsx:3, components/admin/audit/audit-log.tsx:209 and :329, components/admin/features/ai-chats-manager.tsx:165, components/admin/features/queue-status-manager.tsx:8 and components/admin/features/system-settings-manager.tsx:522. The other five are dead: UsersListSkeleton (line 17), AuditLogSkeleton (40), UserDetailSkeleton (63), StaffListSkeleton (96) and TeamsListSkeleton (120). Each was written to mirror the real shape of one admin section while it loads. The file is only reachable through the wildcard barrel components/admin/shared/index.ts:8 ('export * from "./skeleton"'), and no consumer of that barrel imports any of the five: the only occurrence of each of those five identifiers anywhere in the repo is its own declaration line. Dead range is lines 14-139, 126 lines.
impact: The bespoke per-section loading states were built and never wired, so the admin panel shows generic bar/table placeholders that do not match the content that replaces them, producing more layout shift than the author intended. Nobody can tell from the file that these are unwired, because the barrel re-exports them with a wildcard.
recommendation: Either delete lines 14-139 of components/admin/shared/skeleton.tsx (126 lines), or wire each one into its section's loading branch: UsersListSkeleton and UserDetailSkeleton in app/admin/page.tsx, AuditLogSkeleton in components/admin/audit/audit-log.tsx:329, StaffListSkeleton in components/admin/staff/staff-list.tsx, TeamsListSkeleton in the teams tab. Pick one and do not leave both states.

title: The admin email preview reimplements lib/email/email.ts's layout and has already drifted on four elements, so what an admin previews before a broadcast is not what recipients receive
description:
components/admin/shared/email-preview-html.ts:1-15 says what it is: "Client-side stand-in for the real branded email layout (lib/email/email.ts's `layout()`, server-only) ... This mirrors that layout's header, card, and footer; keep the two in step when either changes." generateEmailPreviewHtml (:28-80) renders the srcDoc for the preview iframes in components/admin/features/mass-email-manager.tsx:402 and components/admin/features/email-logs-manager.tsx:414.

The colour half of the mirroring did get consolidated: lib/config/brand.ts is the single palette and both lib/email/email.ts:19-47 (via its COLORS alias) and email-preview-html.ts:17 read it. The markup half has drifted in four ways against lib/email/email.ts's layout() at :106-179:

  1. Logo. layout() uses LOGO_URL, absolutised if relative (:110-113). The preview hardcodes `${appUrl}/favicon.svg` (:55), so a deployment that sets a custom LOGO_URL previews the wrong logo.
  2. Responsive rules. layout() ships a `@media (max-width: 600px)` block with `.vr-shell` and `.vr-card` padding overrides (:135-141) and puts those classes on the elements. The preview has neither, so the preview does not show the mobile rendering.
  3. Preferences button. layout() renders a "Manage email preferences" button whenever an unsubscribeToken is present (:117-129). The preview never renders it.
  4. Support line. layout()'s footer reads "...or reach the team at <SUPPORT_EMAIL>" (:167). The preview's footer stops at "Choose what we send you in your account settings." (:69).

The preview also drops the `<title>`, the `supported-color-schemes` meta and the `a { color }` rule that layout() sets.
impact: An admin composing a broadcast in components/admin/features/mass-email-manager.tsx sees a footer with no unsubscribe control and no support address, then sends a message that has both, and sees the wrong logo if the deployment configured one. The preview also cannot show whether the message survives a 375px viewport, which is where the real layout's media query matters. Low severity because nothing sent is wrong, only what the admin was shown before sending.
recommendation: Export the layout as a pure function of its inputs from a module both sides can import, for example lib/email/layout.ts exporting `emailLayout({ content, appName, appUrl, logoSrc, supportEmail, unsubscribeUrl })` with no server-only imports, and have lib/email/email.ts's layout() and components/admin/shared/email-preview-html.ts both call it. If the server-only boundary makes that awkward, at minimum port the four differences into email-preview-html.ts and add a test that asserts the two produce the same footer and header markup for the same inputs.

title: broadcast_recipients has no UNIQUE(message_id, user_id), so the mass-email send loop uses a read-then-insert guard that two concurrent sends both pass
description: broadcast_recipients (instrumentation.ts:1151-1162) has a surrogate `id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY` and two separate single-column indexes on message_id and user_id, and no uniqueness on the pair. The send handler and the resend handler each compensate in the application, with a comment that says so verbatim: "broadcast_recipients has no unique key, so this is an app-level guard rather than ON CONFLICT" (app/api/v3/admin/features/route.ts:555-557 and the duplicated copy at :717-719). The guard is `SELECT 1 FROM broadcast_recipients WHERE message_id = $1 AND user_id = $2 AND status = 'sent' LIMIT 1` followed, if the select returned nothing, by sendEmail and then a plain INSERT (:559-573 and :721-735). Nothing serialises the two steps, and the same recipient is only marked after the SMTP round trip completes, so the window between the SELECT and the INSERT is the full duration of one email send. Two admins hitting send and resend for the same message, or one admin double-clicking, or the resend path racing a still-running first send, both pass the SELECT for the same recipient and both send.
impact: The whole verified user base can receive the same broadcast twice, from a feature whose stated design goal in that comment is that it must not. AUDIT-012#perf-07 already established that this loop iterates every verified user with no LIMIT and does one SELECT plus one INSERT plus one sequential SMTP call per recipient, so the race window per recipient is large and the number of recipients is unbounded. Duplicate mass email is the fastest way to get a sending domain reputation-flagged.
recommendation: Add `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_broadcast_recipients_message_user ON broadcast_recipients(message_id, user_id);` in instrumentation.ts and replace both read-then-insert blocks with an insert-first claim: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (message_id, user_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING id, send the email only when a row came back, then UPDATE the status. That also satisfies AUDIT-012#perf-15's item (8), which asked for a plain composite index on the same two columns for the read side, so one unique index covers both findings.

title: Two admin log-search endpoints still pass an unescaped ILIKE pattern, unlike the user and team search that were fixed for the same issue
description: app/api/v3/admin/email-logs/route.ts:67-71 does `params.push(`%${search}%`)` then `(recipient ILIKE $n OR subject ILIKE $n)`, and app/api/v3/admin/error-logs/route.ts:61-64 does `WHERE message ILIKE $1 OR detail ILIKE $1` with `[`%${search}%`]`. Neither escapes `%`, `_` or `\` and neither adds `ESCAPE '\'`. The sibling searches were fixed for exactly this: app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:127 (`const searchEscaped = search.replace(/[\\%_]/g, '\\$&')`, with the comment 'Without this, typing "%" returns all users (full table scan)') and app/api/v3/admin/teams/route.ts:37/:58 both use `ESCAPE '\'`. These two were left behind. It is not SQL injection: the value is still a bound parameter.
impact: An admin searching email or error logs for a literal `_` or `%` gets wrong results (every underscore matches any character), and a search of `%` degrades to a full scan of system_error_logs / the email log table, which are the two highest-volume tables in the schema. Bounded to staff users.
recommendation: Apply the same one-line escape used at app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:127 in both files, and add `ESCAPE '\'` to each ILIKE clause, matching app/api/v3/admin/teams/route.ts.

title: Two per-request lookups sit on the admin engine-feedback page that each pull every findings blob for a tag with no LIMIT
category: N+1 with an unbounded inner query
description: `for (const row of counts.rows)` at app/api/v3/admin/engine-feedback/ai-tag-candidates/route.ts:171 puts a `Promise.all` inside the loop (line 172), so the loop itself is fully sequential -- two round trips per candidate tag. The second of those (lines 182-186) is `SELECT sh.findings FROM scan_tags st JOIN scan_history sh ON sh.id = st.scan_id WHERE st.tag = $1 AND st.source = 'ai'` with no LIMIT: it pulls the complete findings JSONB of every scan carrying that tag and then flatMaps the result in JavaScript at line 191.
impact: Staff-only and low frequency, so bounded in blast radius, but the page cost grows with total AI-tagged scan volume and each iteration transfers (scans with that tag) x (full findings blob) bytes. It is the same shape as perf-06's top-vulnerabilities query and will fail the same way at scale.
recommendation: Hoist the `Promise.all` outside the loop so the per-tag queries actually run in parallel, add a `LIMIT` and a recency bound to the query at line 182, and project only the finding fields the candidate scoring reads rather than `sh.findings` whole.

title: broadcast_messages.sent_by is left NULL on a message's initial send, only populated on resend
description: The sent_by column is correctly bound where it's set, but the admin features route only sets it in the resend action branch, never in the initial send path. A broadcast's first send leaves sent_by NULL, so "Sent by X" only appears in the admin UI after a resend.
recommendation: Set sent_by = user.id in the initial send branch too, not just resend.

title: Admin read operations produce no audit trail (AUDIT-004#audit-01 carry-over)
description: Admin GET endpoints (user lookup, team listing, scan history browsing, notification reads) write nothing to admin_audit_log. An insider threat or compromised admin account can exfiltrate user data with no forensic trail.
recommendation: Call logAuditAction for significant read operations (user detail views, bulk exports). Summarize targets rather than logging full payloads.
